title: introduce-telemetry-harmony-and-alert-sway-adapter
author: Sofia Patel
description: Motivation: Reduce noisy alert churn and speed SRE RCA by fusing metrics, spans, and sampled logs into a lightweight per-invocation signal vector and using that vector to drive an adaptive alert thresholding mechanism (the 'Sway' adapter). This PR implements a telemetry fusion layer (Telemetry Harmony) that performs per-invocation feature extraction (token-phase durations, model variant tags, kv-cache hit/miss counters, kernel-queue latencies) and exposes a compact signal envelope. It also introduces the Sway adapter which consumes historical envelopes and applies noise-aware smoothing to alert thresholds and alert-suppression windows. Changes: 1) observability/harmony: new aggregator service (Go) that consumes existing metric/tracing streams, emits compact "envelopes" to the observability pipeline; 2) observability/adapter/sway: Python adapter that provides adaptive thresholds via a configurable sliding ensemble and exposes an HTTP policy endpoint for alert evaluators; 3) dashboard: new Signal Harmony Explorer panel (Grafana JSON) that shows per-route signal envelopes, alert-sway recommendations, and a drift timeline; 4) alerting: new alert rules that optionally call the Sway policy endpoint to get calibrated thresholds; 5) tests: unit + integration harness, synthetic replay scripts for regression testing; 6) docs: observability guide describing operational considerations and rollout plan. Checklist: [x] design doc referenced (ENG-1843) [x] unit tests added [x] integration replay harness [x] metrics/traces/log sampling knobs exposed [ ] long-term retention/backfill plan (follow-up) Rollout plan: start behind a feature flag in observability ingest path, run telemetry harmony in parallel to existing rollups for 48 hours to validate parity, enable Sway adapter read-only mode in eval environment (alerts not suppressed) for 1 week, then enable suppression with conservative decay window. Rollback: feature flags for ingestion and suppression; stop adapter and revert to static thresholds. Why unique: instead of only adding new metrics or dashboards, this PR constructs a compact cross-signal representation and plugs it into alerting logic to substantially reduce false positives on noisy token-level signals while preserving high-signal incidents. Related: ENG-1910 (alert tuning), SUP-4122 incident reproducer. Impact: In internal perf tests with synthetic storms we saw alert volume drop ~42% for token-phase noisy routes with <1% reduction in true positive detection in the RCA window. Operational cost: small CPU overhead on ingest nodes (~3-5%), modest storage for envelopes (~5% of metric volume).
commits: Add harmony aggregator and envelope schema
Implement sway adapter and HTTP policy server
Grafana: add Signal Harmony Explorer panel
Add alert rules and Sway integration hooks
tests: add replay harness and unit tests
reviewer_comments: Ava Martinez: This looks promising. Can you add a short description of the envelope schema in the PR body? Also double-check the concurrency model in aggregator.go; ingest nodes are sensitive to goroutine explosion.
Tomás Li: Sway policy endpoint should have a circuit-breaker and a cached fallback. What happens if the adapter is down?
Rachel Chen: Dashboard looks useful, but the panel's query is expensive when showing 30d. Could we add a decimated/overview-only query for longer ranges?
author_responses: Sofia Patel: Added envelope.proto and a short schema blurb in docs. Aggregator uses a bounded worker pool and backpressure on the ingest channel, added comments and tests for concurrency limits.
Sofia Patel: Implemented a local LRU cache and a 500ms timeout plus circuit-breaker on the Sway client; default fallback returns static thresholds and is configurable via env var.
Sofia Patel: Added an 'overview' toggle to the panel which switches to downsampled rollups for ranges >72h; noted performance guidance in the dashboard README.
release_notes:
- Add Telemetry Harmony: compact per-invocation signal envelopes
- Add Sway adapter: adaptive alert thresholding for noisy token-level signals
- New Grafana panel: Signal Harmony Explorer for cross-signal debugging
- Opt-in rollout behind feature flags; follow upgrade notes in docs/observability/signal_harmony.md
